blocks.text: Macrophages develop from monocytes (a type of white blood cells). A macrophage ingests a bacterium, by endocytosis, and kills it by its lysozyme enzymes. Some macrophages are fixed within some organs e.g., lungs, liver, spleen, and brain. But most of them patrol in the blood, lymph and interstitial fluid.

blocks.alt: A large pink macrophage with a ruffled surface and a long extension reaching to the upper right, on a dark teal background, surrounded by yellow rod-shaped bacteria; one bacterium is being taken in at its upper edge.
